ev.q: Swaziland had high reported prevalence of sexual violence among females (37.6%).
Patterns in the prevalence of any form of childhood sexual violence differed by country
The prevalence of childhood sexual violence among females was ≥25% in five of seven countries surveyed.
In most countries surveyed, the proportion of victims that received services, including health and child protective services, was ≤10.0%.
Cambodia reported the lowest rates for both females (4.4%) and males (5.6%).
Swaziland had the largest proportion (24.0%) of females receiving services.
VACS are a multistage cluster survey with national coverage
The results of this study provide nationally representative estimates by which countries can measure their progress
